title: Cut elimination for equality-free first-order sequents

based_on.title: Proof Theory 2018: Sequent calculus for predicate logic (handout 9)

summary: Remove cuts from actual equality-free quantified sequent trees, relate the result to pure classical deductions, and retain substitution instances of endsequent subformulas.
abstract: A cut joins a proof offering a formula to a proof offering its opposite, then removes both offers. We show how to replace every such join by the seven original equality-free first-order sequent rules. The construction handles repeated formulas in finite-set contexts and replaces protected parameters by the actual witness terms used by existential rules. It gives exact correspondence with classical natural deductions whose equality rules are disabled, preserves the distinction between raw proofs and proofs with auxiliary names, and makes every formula in the resulting tree an actual substitution instance of an endsequent subformula.
